title: Understanding Model Instability
text: Model instability in validation accuracy can often be attributed to the variability in the data used for training and validation. This can lead to overfitting or underfitting, depending on the model's complexity and the data distribution.

title: Exploring Cross-Validation
text: Cross-validation is a technique used to assess how the results of a statistical analysis will generalize to an independent data set. It is mainly used in settings where the goal is prediction, and one wants to estimate how accurately a predictive model will perform in practice.

title: Implementing Cross-Validation
text: To implement cross-validation, you can divide your dataset into k subsets, or 'folds'. Train the model on k-1 of these folds and validate it on the remaining fold. Repeat this process k times, each time using a different fold as the validation set.
choices: Retrain with more data in the training set allocated to the validation set.
Retrain with more data in the validation set allocated to the training set.
Add more features to the dataset, to increase model complexity.
